note: Mermaid theming for every diagram. One SVG per source, or one frame per step for a series, transparent canvas, every node carrying its own fill, so the same file reads on the dark notebook, on GitHub in either mode, in VS Code and in Colab. Palette is lwp-website .dark.
themeCSS: .edgeLabel, .edgeLabel p, .edgeLabel span { color: #A8A29E; } .cluster text, .cluster span { fill: #A8A29E; }

frames.note: How render_diagrams.py cuts a step series into frames. Colour always means role, weight always means time: a dashed ghost is not reached yet, a glow in the role's own colour is what this step added.
frames.sizeReason: The renderer writes each SVG at the size that fits this box, so the picture fits a laptop window in VS Code, GitHub and Colab, none of which load custom.css. Fit wins over label size. A frame that must shrink until its labels are under minLabelPx fails check-diagrams, and the fix is a shorter source or a cut node, never a bigger box.

roleMeaning.input: something arriving from outside, usually untrusted
roleMeaning.store: durable state, a database, a queue or a file
roleMeaning.decision: a branch, a gate or a human approval
roleMeaning.risk: where it goes wrong, the failure being taught
roleMeaning.output: what the system returns or commits
